note: Immutable. A change to any number, source or assumption is a NEW dated file (factors-YYYY-MM-DD.json) that the page then reads; this file is never edited. The page reads every number from the file it names in /carbon/carbon.js (FACTORS_FILE). Visitor ZIPs are never logged or stored.
quantity: kg CO2e = billable short tons x miles x emission factor (kg CO2e per short ton-mile), summed leg by leg. Transport only; production, packaging, factory-to-Houston and last-metre are not counted.

truck.label: Medium- and heavy-duty truck, per short ton-mile

source.title: U.S. EPA, GHG Emission Factors Hub, January 2025 edition
source.table: Table 8, Scope 3 Category 4, row 'Medium- and Heavy-Duty Truck' (short ton-mile)

source.title: U.S. EPA, GHG Emission Factors Hub, January 2025 edition
source.table: Table 8, Scope 3 Category 4, row 'Waterborne Craft' (short ton-mile)
source.boundary: combustion only; a U.S. average for all waterborne freight, not container ships specifically

source.title: U.S. EPA, GHG Emission Factors Hub, January 2025 edition
source.table: Table 11, Global Warming Potential (GWP), rows CO2, CH4, N2O

circuity.use: truck miles = great-circle miles x factor

source.title: Qureshi, Hwang & Chin (2002), Comparison of Distance Estimates for Commodity Flow Survey: Great Circle Distances Versus Network-Based Distances
source.table: Transportation Research Record 1804, 212-216: a constant circuity factor of 1.22 gave unbiased distance estimates (single trips can differ widely)

density.derivation: payload_lb / trailer_cuft = 44000 / 3800 = 11.58, rounded to 11.6: the density at which a 53 ft dry van fills by weight and by space together. Billable weight = max(actual lb, cubic ft x 11.6).

source.title: Hale Trailer, Dry Van Dimensions & Capacity Guide
source.table: 53 ft dry van: about 3,800-4,000 cu ft and 44,000-45,000 lb payload (lower ends used)

houston.what: ZCTA 77020 internal point, our Houston warehouse

source.title: U.S. Census Bureau 2026 Gazetteer, ZCTA file

port.what: Port of Long Beach, CA (approximate port coordinates)

shanghai.what: Shanghai (assumed origin port of an import)

source.title: approximate city coordinates, set by us

buyer_table.derivation: Per 3-digit ZIP prefix: mean of the Census ZCTA internal points (INTPTLAT, INTPTLONG), weighted by land area (ALAND), rounded to 2 decimals.

source.title: U.S. Census Bureau, 2026 Gazetteer Files, ZIP Code Tabulation Areas (2026_Gaz_zcta_national.zip)

geometry.no_truck_why: Lower 48 only: trucks do not reach AK, HI, PR or Guam; APO/FPO prefixes are not in the table.

cube.reference_what: typical 10x10 kitchen = 25 linear feet (about 12 ft base + 13 ft wall): SB36, B36, B30, B24, B18 and wall cabinets 2xW3630, 2xW3030, W2430. Other sizes scale per linear foot.

flat.how: One pallet of ready-to-assemble cartons. From our freight sizing model (cube.py in our operations code), checked against closed orders' bills of lading: weight within 3%, space within 11%.

assembled.how: box_cuft = sum of each cabinet's outside box with 2 in added each way (catalog dimensions). Space = box_cuft / efficiency (stacking gaps) x deck (10% for the pallet deck) = about 165 cu ft. Weight = cabinet_lb + pallet_lb x space / pallet_cuft = about 770 lb. Our assumption, not a measured shipment.

import_route.legs: container ship Shanghai to Port of Long Beach (great-circle distance, about 6,500 miles, a minimum: ships sail further), then truck Long Beach to the buyer (distance x circuity).
import_route.ship_weight: actual weight (flat-pack lb), not billable weight
import_route.not_counted: the leg from the factory to the Chinese port; transport to Houston for the Houston routes
import_route.supplier: generic import, not any particular supplier's cabinets or ours
import_route.distance_source: great-circle between the two ports' coordinates; we did not find a published port-to-port table we could verify

disclosures: Starts at our Houston warehouse (77020); transport to Houston is not counted.
Transport only: not making the cabinets, packaging production, factory-to-Houston, assembly, disposal or your own trips.
Estimates, roughly +/-10-20% from the sizing alone and more from the factors and routes.
The ship factor is an all-waterborne U.S. average (could be high for container ships); the ship distance is a straight-line minimum (low). We cannot say which effect is larger.
If weight alone counted, flat-pack and assembled would tie, because the cabinets weigh about the same.
No claim about total environmental impact, only the transport numbers shown.

changelog.change: First versioned factors file. Values are those of the first /carbon/ release (2026-10-31): EPA Hub 2025 Tables 8 and 11, circuity 1.22, 11.6 lb per cu ft, Census 2026 gazetteer. Source tables snapshotted under /carbon/sources/2026-10-31/.
